source_book: NCERT Class 11 Ch.5 Laws of Motion — table-of-contents reference only (Newton's second law is its own section, immediately after the first law, before constraint/pulley problems); teaching authored from first principles. The atomic idea: a net force gives a body ACCELERATION — proportional to the force and inversely proportional to the mass (a = ΣF/m) — and only that. Does NOT cover why zero net force means constant velocity (newton_first_law), force pairs (newton_third_law), drawing all forces on a body (free_body_diagram), friction or inclines (block_on_incline), or the vector/arbitrary-direction form of the law (newton_second_law_direction, advisory only). Engine: the shared newtons_laws_body field_3d scenario (docs/NEWTONS_LAWS_BODY_ENGINE_SPEC.md) — a flat frictionless surface (theta_deg = 0, mu = 0 throughout) carrying two independent bodies (no pulley) in the mass/force compare states, one body in the single-body states. All four states are expressible with the engine's existing config surface; ENGINE GAP: none.

real_world_anchor.primary: An elevator starting to rise — the motor applies a steady extra force, and for those first moments you feel the floor press harder while the elevator's speed climbs from zero; the same steady force, speed rising the whole time it acts.
real_world_anchor.secondary: Pushing a loaded luggage cart versus an empty one with the same effort — the empty cart gains speed twice as fast; the load didn't change your push, it changed what your push achieves.

aha_moment.statement: A force does not give speed — it gives a rate of gaining speed.
aha_moment.visual_confirmation: The applied-force arrow F never changes length and the acceleration readout a never moves, yet the velocity readout v climbs every single second without limit — force sets a RATE, not a speed.

m2.name: mass of body B (mass-compare slider, STATE_2)

F_net.name: net force
F_net.derived: F (identical to F_applied; theta = 0 and mu = 0 all concept)

constraints: theta = 0 and mu_s = mu_k = 0 in every state of this concept (flat, frictionless floor throughout)
F_net = F_applied at every instant this concept authors (no incline component, no friction to subtract)
under a constant applied force, a is exactly constant and v grows without bound before any clamp
mass and force are independent knobs: doubling m halves a at fixed F; doubling F doubles a at fixed m
mu_s/mu_k and theta are never authored nonzero here — that scope belongs to block_on_incline / friction_static_kinetic
STOP_EPS_V = 0.01 m/s is carried from the shared integrator but never binds in the three guided states (drive != 0 whenever F != 0); it can bind only in the S4 sandbox default F = 0

STATE_1.title: Steady force, from rest: a pins, v never stops climbing

scene_composition.text: Constant force from rest: watch which reading moves
a pins at 0.10 from frame 1 and never moves; v climbs every second
like an elevator's motor pushing you upward — the floor presses harder, speed keeps rising

tts_sentences.text_en: Last time, with no force, speed stayed frozen.
Now watch this force arrow F, switched on, never changing length.
From rest, the block's speed climbs every second, yet the acceleration reading a never moves.
A steady force doesn't set a speed — it sets a rate of change.

misconception_watch.belief: A constant force produces a constant speed — force is what velocity is made of (the everyday default: steadily pushed furniture moves at steady speed, because hidden friction cancels the push).
misconception_watch.visual_counter: The force arrow F never changes length and the acceleration reading a never changes value, yet the velocity reading v climbs every single second without limit — the wrong expectation (v flat) is directly contradicted by the live readout pair.
misconception_watch.one_line_fix: Force sets acceleration, not velocity — hold the force and the speed keeps climbing.

STATE_2.title: Same force, different mass: double the mass, half the acceleration

scene_composition.text: Two identical force arrows — only the mass differs
m₂ carries twice the mass — a reads exactly half, 0.10 vs 0.20
drag the m₂ slider — its acceleration reading changes live, mid-run

tts_sentences.text_en: Two identical force arrows — same length, same force F — launch two blocks together.
The heavier one, m two, carries twice the mass and visibly falls behind, its acceleration reading exactly half the lighter block's.
Drag the m two slider heavier or lighter and watch its acceleration change live, right on the readout.

misconception_watch.belief: The same push moves everything the same way — mass doesn't really matter, heavy things are just slower to get going.
misconception_watch.visual_counter: Two IDENTICAL force arrows, the only difference is mass — and the double-mass block gets exactly half the acceleration at every instant (a readouts 0.20 vs 0.10, distances in a 2:1 ratio).
misconception_watch.one_line_fix: Mass is resistance to acceleration — double the mass, half the acceleration.

STATE_3.title: Same mass, different force: double the force, double the acceleration

scene_composition.text: Now equal masses — the force arrow on m₂ is doubled
m₂'s force arrow is drawn twice as long — a reads exactly double, 0.20 vs 0.10
same gap as before, made by force this time — one law, two dials: a = F/m

tts_sentences.text_en: Same two blocks, now equal in mass — but m two's force arrow is drawn twice as long: double the push.
Its acceleration reading is exactly double m one's.
Same gap as before, this time made by force, not mass — one law, two different dials, both reading a equals F over m.

STATE_4.title: Explore: drive m, F, v₀ — watch a obey a = ΣF/m live

scene_composition.text: Set mass, force, v₀ — watch v, a, F, ΣF respond live
double m, watch a halve; reverse F's sign, watch it brake then reverse

tts_sentences.text_en: Your turn — set mass, force, and starting speed, and watch acceleration respond live, always obeying a equals F over m.
